name: Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare
description: Microbes in household foods, industrial products, antibiotics, sewage treatment, biogas, biocontrol and biofertilisers

cards.definition: Everywhere: soil, water, air, inside bodies; even in thermal vents (~100 °C), deep soil, under snow, highly acidic places
Protozoa, bacteria, fungi, microscopic plant and animal viruses, viroids and prions
Proteinaceous infectious agents

cards.term: Identify the bacterial shapes in Figure 8.1.
cards.definition: (a) Rod-shaped (b) spherical (both ×1500) (c) rod-shaped with flagella (×50,000)
(a) Bacteriophage (b) Adenovirus (respiratory infections) (c) rod-shaped TMV

cards.term: How can bacteria and fungi be seen with the naked eye?
cards.definition: Grown on nutritive media as colonies

cards.term: Correction: NCERT prints the vent temperature as "1000C". Correct?
cards.definition: 100 °C (degree sign lost in printing)

cards.term: Microbes that convert milk to curd?
cards.definition: Lactobacillus and others: lactic acid bacteria (LAB)
Produces acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins

cards.term: What is the "starter" in curd making?
cards.definition: A small amount of curd containing millions of LAB, used as inoculum

cards.term: Nutritional benefit of curd over milk?
cards.definition: Increased vitamin B₁₂

cards.term: Role of LAB in our stomach?
cards.definition: Checks disease-causing microbes

cards.term: Why does idli/dosa dough puff up?
cards.definition: Bacterial fermentation produces CO₂
Baker’s yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Traditional drink of southern India made by fermenting palm sap

cards.term: Foods made by microbial fermentation (besides curd, bread)?
cards.definition: Fermented fish, soyabean, bamboo-shoots; cheese

cards.term: What makes the large holes in Swiss cheese?
cards.definition: CO₂ from the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii
By growing a specific fungus on it for flavour
Wheat: bread, bhatura. Rice: idli, dosa. Bengal gram: dhokla, khaman.

cards.term: Sample to show microbes under a microscope (Exercise 1)?
cards.definition: Curd: full of LAB, easy to carry and observe
Fermentors
Saccharomyces cerevisiae (brewer’s yeast)

cards.term: What does brewer’s yeast ferment, and product?
cards.definition: Malted cereals and fruit juices → ethanol

cards.term: Beverages made without vs with distillation?
cards.definition: Without: wine, beer. With: whisky, brandy, rum.
"Wise Boys Run" (Whisky, Brandy, Rum) to the still
"Against life" (of pathogens); pro-life for humans
Chemicals produced by some microbes that kill or retard growth of other (disease-causing) microbes

cards.term: First antibiotic, and who discovered it?
cards.definition: Penicillin, Alexander Fleming (chance discovery)
A mould in an unwashed Staphylococci plate prevented bacterial growth around it
Penicillium notatum
Ernest Chain and Howard Florey
1945: Fleming, Chain and Florey; used to treat soldiers in World War II
Plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu), leprosy (kusht rog)
Penicillium notatum (penicillin) and Cephalosporium (cephalosporin)

cards.term: Why is overuse of antibiotics dangerous? (intuition)
cards.definition: It selects resistant bacteria (evolution in action), making antibiotics useless
Citric acid: Aspergillus niger (fungus); Acetic acid: Acetobacter aceti (bacterium); Butyric acid: Clostridium butylicum (bacterium); Lactic acid: Lactobacillus (bacterium)

cards.definition: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
In detergents: remove oily stains

cards.term: Why are bottled juices clearer than homemade?
cards.definition: Clarified by pectinases and proteases

cards.term: What is streptokinase and its use?
cards.definition: From Streptococcus, modified by genetic engineering; clot buster for myocardial infarction patients
Fungus Trichoderma polysporum; immunosuppressant in organ transplants
Yeast Monascus purpureus; lower blood cholesterol by competitively inhibiting its synthesis enzyme
Streptokinase: Streptococcus; Cyclosporin A: Trichoderma polysporum; Statins: Monascus purpureus; Penicillin: Penicillium notatum

Source?

Cyclosporin ATrichoderma polysporum
StatinsMonascus purpureus

cards.definition: Transplant drug from Trichoderma; cholesterol drug from Monascus (Mind your heart)
Municipal waste water, largely human excreta; rich in organic matter and microbes (many pathogenic)

cards.term: Why can’t sewage go directly into rivers? (Exercise 7)
cards.definition: It is pathogenic and rich in organic matter: pollutes water, depletes O₂, spreads water-borne diseases
Heterotrophic microbes naturally present in sewage
Physical removal of particles by filtration and sedimentation
Floating debris removed by sequential filtration; grit removed by sedimentation → primary sludge + effluent
Primary effluent is agitated and aerated in aeration tanks, growing aerobic microbes into flocs
Masses of bacteria with fungal filaments forming mesh-like structures

cards.term: Key difference: primary vs secondary treatment (Exercise 8)?
cards.definition: Primary: physical. Secondary: biological (microbes consume organic matter).
Amount of O₂ consumed if all organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria
Indirect measure of organic matter; higher BOD = more polluting potential
Sediment of bacterial flocs in the settling tank after BOD is reduced
Small part → back to aeration tank as inoculum; major part → anaerobic sludge digesters

cards.term: What happens in anaerobic sludge digesters?
cards.definition: Anaerobic bacteria digest bacteria and fungi, producing biogas (methane, H₂S, CO₂)
Released into rivers and streams

cards.term: Aerial view of an STP (Figure 8.7): circular tanks are?
cards.definition: Settling/aeration tanks of a sewage treatment plant

cards.text: Sewage treatment flow: {{c1::primary treatment (filtration, sedimentation)}} → {{c2::aeration tank (flocs)}} → {{c3::settling tank (activated sludge)}} → {{c4::anaerobic sludge digester (biogas)}}.

cards.definition: C sewage, A secondary effluent, B river water

cards.term: Plans to save Indian rivers from sewage?
cards.definition: Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan (Ministry of Environment and Forests)

cards.term: Why is untreated sewage still discharged?
cards.definition: Sewage production rose with urbanisation but STPs did not increase enough
Mixture of gases, predominantly methane, produced by microbes; used as fuel
Anaerobic bacteria producing methane (with CO₂, H₂) from cellulosic material; Methanobacterium
Anaerobic sludge of sewage and the rumen of cattle
Help break down cellulose; important for cattle nutrition

cards.term: Why is gobar good for biogas?
cards.definition: Cattle dung is rich in methanogens
Concrete tank 10–15 ft deep with dung slurry floating cover rises as gas forms gas outlet pipe spent slurry outlet (used as fertiliser)

cards.term: Why are biogas plants mostly rural?
cards.definition: Cattle dung is plentiful there
Cooking and lighting

cards.term: Who developed biogas technology in India?
cards.definition: IARI and KVIC (Khadi and Village Industries Commission)

cards.term: Can microbes be a source of energy? (Exercise 9)
cards.definition: Yes: methanogens produce biogas (methane) from dung and waste; yeast makes ethanol
CO₂ in dough, Swiss cheese; methane, CO₂, H₂S in biogas
Use of biological methods to control plant diseases and pests
Toxic to humans and animals; pollute soil, groundwater, fruits, vegetables, crops
Keep pests at manageable levels, not eradicated; eradication is undesirable as predators depend on them
Biodiversity furthers health
Ladybird: aphids. Dragonflies: mosquitoes.
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)

cards.term: How is Bt applied and how does it act?
cards.definition: Dried spores mixed with water, sprayed on plants eaten by larvae toxin released in the gut kills them other insects unharmed

cards.term: Example of Bt toxin genes in crops?
cards.definition: Bt-cotton

cards.term: Fungal biocontrol agent of plant diseases?
cards.definition: Trichoderma: free-living in root ecosystems
Pathogens of insects and arthropods; used as biocontrol agents
Nucleopolyhedrovirus

cards.term: Why are baculoviruses good biocontrol agents?
cards.definition: Species-specific, narrow spectrum; no harm to plants, mammals, birds, fish or non-target insects
Integrated pest management: conserves beneficial insects; baculoviruses suit it
"Bt Treats Bugs": Bacillus thuringiensis, Trichoderma, Baculovirus
Organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of soil
Bacteria, fungi, cyanobacteria
Rhizobium in root nodules
Azospirillum and Azotobacter
Glomus
Fungus absorbs phosphorus for the plant resistance to root pathogens tolerance to salinity and drought better growth

cards.term: What does the fungus gain from mycorrhiza? (think)
cards.definition: Food (sugars) and shelter from the plant root
Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria
Paddy fields
Add organic matter to soil, increasing fertility

cards.term: How do microbes reduce chemical fertilisers and pesticides? (Exercise 10)
cards.definition: Biofertilisers fix N and supply P; biocontrol agents (Bt, Trichoderma, baculovirus) kill pests
Rhizobium: Symbiotic N₂-fixing bacterium; Azotobacter, Azospirillum: Free-living N₂-fixing bacteria; Glomus: Mycorrhizal fungus (P uptake); Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria: N₂-fixing cyanobacteria
